text:
Nina: tossing a sketch into the channel: instead of full VPC peering per-customer, what if we publish a minimal control-plane API surface clients run locally (a 'lite agent') and keep data-plane egress via shared endpoints? pros/cons?
Omar: benefit = fewer cross-account routes, quicker onboards. downside = more state on customer side and harder audit centralization.
Felix: important: decide which control APIs are "local-only" vs "central-only". local-only = health probes, short-term cache of routing decisions. central-only = billing, customer ACLs.
Gwen: agree. also think about the trust model. if agent can act without peering, central must have signed manifests and attestations to prevent spoofing.
Nina: attestation idea: signed manifest + short-lived bootstrap token. agent verifies manifests with central CA. revocations pushed via signed delta stream.
Omar: delta stream is OK but what about out-of-order delivery? stubs must enforce sequence numbers + monotonic checks. add checksum+signature per diff.
Felix: operationally, local agents mean we need local logs/metrics buffer that ships on reconnect. encrypted buffer is fine. but we need retention and purge policies for GDPR.
Gwen: on egress: shared endpoints should support source-ip preservation where required. options: (1) reserved ENI per customer, (2) 1:1 NAT mapping with sticky leases, (3) tunnel to customer-owned exit. each has tradeoffs.
Nina: tunnel to customer-owned exit is neat for full control but requires customer infra and increases latency. reserved ENI is easiest for customer allowlists but scales poorly.
Omar: sticky lease NAT is attractive if we can guarantee lease handover semantics. need ARP/neighbor flusher + pre-warm so we don't drop long-lived TCP. worst-case: small window of resets; document recommended client retries.
Felix: also consider L7 routing constraints: if we do SNI passthrough we avoid MITM cert issues but lose payload visibility for routing. approach: use SNI + header hints and require customers to opt-in to payload inspection for advanced routing.
Gwen: compliance: for some regs we cannot touch private keys. agent model helps, keep TLS termination on customer side and only route by SNI/ALPN. central must not request keys. add this as non-negotiable.
sec-bot: flagged: security-checklist-missing (agent-auth, revocation-flow, key-handling). run 'sec-audit agent-proposal'
Nina: proposal for next RFC: 1) define minimal control-plane API surface and ACLs 2) describe bootstrap and attestation flows 3) enumerate egress options with cost/latency matrix 4) failure modes (agent drift, lost central, lease transfer) 5) runbook for forced-revocation
Omar: I'll draft the lease transfer design (how to pre-warm, ARP/ND, TCP drain, and monitoring). Felix: can you do the attestation/security appendix? Gwen: please add compliance constraints from enterprise customers.
Felix: will include signed diff format + sequence rules. plan to prototype a small go agent that consumes diffs.
Gwen: will collect examples of customers that require ENI today so we can size cost model.
Nina: let's aim to have draft up by next Tues. ping me for quick review. thanks all :rocket:
